cluster_summary: This cluster consists of 15 CVEs involving improper handling of untrusted data during XML/DOM operations. The vulnerabilities fall into three main categories: unescaped or unvalidated user input in XML serialization leading to injection; unbounded recursion or stack overflow due to missing depth guards; and insufficient controls on XML entity expansion enabling denial of service. Two additional CVEs are outliers involving quadratic time complexity and regex injection.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-influenced inputs, resource identities, state values, or configuration described by the member CVEs into the sensitive operation or security boundary described by the member CVEs. Report code paths where the required validation, authorization, isolation, state check, or binding is absent or not connected to the sensitive effect. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 4 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should Add validation or escaping of user input before inclusion in XML serialization; for example, validate element names against allowed characters, escape CDATA terminators, reject comments containing '-->', validate DocumentType fields against XML grammar, and escape PI closing sequences..

sub_patterns.name: Unescaped or unvalidated user input in XML serialization
sub_patterns.root_cause: User-controlled data is directly inserted into XML output (element/attribute names, comments, CDATA, processing instructions, DocumentType fields) without proper escaping or validation against XML syntax constraints, allowing injection of arbitrary markup.
